title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر في منبر الجمعة عن نصرة المصطفى عليه أزكى الصلاة والسلام
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures from the Friday Pulpit on Supporting the Chosen One, upon him be the purest blessings and peace
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين محاضرة علمية هامة تحت عنوان: "نصرة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم" بمنبر الجمعة في مسجد الذكر بتنسويلم مساء أمس الجمعة 05 ذو القعدة 1433هـ الموافق: 21 سبتمبر 2012.وقد جرت المحاضرة وسط حضور جماهيري كبير غصت به جوانب المسجد وامتلأت به الساحات المحيطة به، حيث توافد الحضور من الساعات الأولى من المساء، وتوالى قدومهم حتى قبيل المغرب، إذ اكتظ داخل المسجد والساحات الموالية له، قبل أن يلجأ الجمهور إلى بعض الحيطان المجاورة، لينتظموا في جلوسهم متعطشين لحضور الشيخ والاستماع لما سيلقيه على آذانهم من العلم الشرعي، ونصرة سيِّد البشرية بعد هذه الهجمات المتوالية من الغرب على مكانته صلى الله عليه وسلم، من خلال قراءات ووقفات رائعة مع سيرته صلى الله عليه وسلم، وتحرى الحضور حتى أمن على دعاء الشيخ في نهاية المحاضرة التي استمرت حتى دخول وقت المغرب. ومن ضمن الوقفات التي تناولتها المحاضرة المواضيع التالية: • خطر ابتعاد الأمة عن نصرة الله ورسوله • لا بد للأمة أن تراجع حساباتها مع الله • الدول التي وقعت فيها الإساءة يتحمل حكامها كامل الضرر المترتب على هذا الفعل الشنيع • استعداد المسلمين جميعا للتضحية نصرة لنبيهم • كل هذه الإساءات لن تضر خير البرية بل تزيده حبا في النفوس • الاستغراب والاستنكار من هذا التمالئ والتتابع في الإساءة • ما يقع في هذه الأزمنة من التطاول على خير البربة هو امتحان للعباد • مواقف الناس اتجاه هذه الابتلاءات، أربعة: • الموقف الأول: موقف الصرحاء من المنافقين • الموقف الثاني: موقف المخذلين • الموقف الثالث: موقف ضعفة الإيمان من العامة • الموقف الرابع: موقف أهل الإيمان الصادقين • أسباب محبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم • سبل الاحتجاج السلمي ونماذجه من سيرة الخلفاء والتابعين وقد دعا الشيخ الددو في نهاية المحاضرة إلى نصرة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من خلال قراءة سيرته وتعليمها للناس، ونشرها في البيوت، والتمسك بسنته، والإحتجاج السلمي، مذكرا بأهمية كتاب "الشفاء" للقاضى عياض في هذا المضمار. محاضرة هامة تطرقت لنقاط كثيرة في سبل نصرة المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام والطرق الناجعة في مواجهة هذه المواقف الحرجة للأمة الإسلامية. لمشاهدة المحاضرة اضغط على الرابط: هنا
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, president of the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education, and president of Abdullah ibn Yasin University — delivered an important scholarly lecture under the title "Supporting the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace", from the Friday pulpit at the Mosque of Remembrance in Tensweilim, on the evening of yesterday, Friday 5 Dhu al-Qa'dah 1433 AH, corresponding to 21 September 2012.

The lecture took place amid a large public attendance which filled the sides of the mosque to overflowing and filled the squares surrounding it. Those attending began arriving from the first hours of the evening and continued to come until shortly before sunset, so that the inside of the mosque and the squares adjoining it were packed, before the crowd resorted to some of the neighbouring walls, arranging themselves in their seating, thirsting to be present with the Sheikh and to hear what he would deliver to their ears of the knowledge of the Sharia — and thirsting for the support of the master of humankind after these successive attacks from the West upon his standing, may God bless him and grant him peace, by way of splendid readings of, and pauses with, his biography (sīrah), may God bless him and grant him peace. Those present persevered to the point of saying amen to the Sheikh's supplication at the close of the lecture, which continued until the time of the sunset prayer came in.

Among the pauses the lecture took up were the following subjects:

- The danger of the community's drawing away from supporting God and His Messenger.
- The community must review its accounts with God.
- The rulers of the states in which the offence occurred bear in full the harm consequent upon this hideous act.
- The readiness of all Muslims to sacrifice in support of their Prophet.
- All these offences will not harm the best of creation; rather they increase the love of him in people's souls.
- Astonishment at, and denunciation of, this collusion and this succession of offences.
- What occurs in these times by way of insolence towards the best of creation is a test for God's servants.
- People's positions towards these trials are four:
- The first position: the position of the avowed among the hypocrites.
- The second position: the position of those who sap others' resolve.
- The third position: the position of the weak in faith among the general public.
- The fourth position: the position of the people of true faith.
- The causes of love for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
- The means of peaceful protest, and its models from the lives of the caliphs and the Successors.

At the end of the lecture Sheikh al-Dedew called for the support of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by reading his biography and teaching it to people, spreading it in the home, holding fast to his sunnah, and peaceful protest — recalling the importance of the book al-Shifāʾ of Qadi Iyad in this field.

An important lecture, which addressed many points on the means of supporting the Chosen One, upon him be blessings and peace, and on the effective ways of confronting these critical situations for the Islamic community.

flags.arabic: الدول التي وقعت فيها الإساءة يتحمل حكامها كامل الضرر المترتب على هذا الفعل الشنيع
flags.context: one heading in the list of the lecture's topics
options: translate faithfully and refer the publication decision upward
translate and publish as ordinary content
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, style guide section 12, and the sharpest line in the record. As a bare heading it asserts that the rulers of the states where the offence took place bear in full the harm that followed from it — which in the autumn of 2012, with embassies attacked and people killed, is a statement about responsibility for those consequences. The Arabic يتحمل الضرر can mean bearing liability for harm or bearing the brunt of it, and the heading gives no clue which, nor what the Sheikh said under it. The English keeps 'bear in full the harm' rather than resolving it into 'are liable for'. Note that record 805, from four days earlier, has him calling attacks on embassies and the killing of protected persons barbaric; the two must be read together, and neither should be published alone.

flags.arabic: مواقف الناس اتجاه هذه الابتلاءات، أربعة: الصرحاء من المنافقين / المخذلين / ضعفة الإيمان من العامة / أهل الإيمان الصادقين
flags.context: the fourfold division in this lecture, against the different fourfold division in record 805
options: render both divisions as served and flag the difference
treat them as the same scheme
flags.note: Two different fourfold classifications of the same episode, four days apart, in the same slice. Record 805's fatwa divides people by their RESPONSE — indifference, violence, objection to protest, legitimate protest. This lecture divides them by their STANDING — avowed hypocrites, those who sap resolve, the weak in faith, the people of true faith. A reader meeting both will assume they map onto each other, so that, for instance, whoever objects to protest is being called a hypocrite. Nothing in either record supports that mapping and the English must not suggest it. The terms here are also far graver than the fatwa's: 'hypocrite' is a category of unbelief. What the Sheikh actually said under each heading is not in the corpus.

flags.context: the second of the four positions
flags.note: takhdhīl is holding others back from an undertaking by talking down its prospects; the Qur'anic register attaches it to the hypocrites at the expedition of Tabuk. 'Defeatists' imports a modern political colour, 'discouragers' is too mild for a word that sits between hypocrisy and weakness of faith in a graded list. 'Those who sap others' resolve' is used. Not in the glossary.

flags.arabic: وقد جرت المحاضرة وسط حضور جماهيري كبير ... حتى دخول وقت المغرب
flags.context: the second paragraph, against records 795 and 797
options: translate in full and flag as boilerplate
flags.note: The third occurrence of this paragraph in this slice, after records 795 and 797, and this time the boilerplate has been edited: a clause about supporting the Prophet after the attacks from the West has been spliced into the middle of it, which is why the sentence now hangs awkwardly on 'thirsting'. That confirms it is a template the desk fills in rather than a description of any particular evening. Translated in full, as the style guide requires, and flagged so the site does not present it as observation.

flags.context: the work recommended at the close
flags.note: al-Shifāʾ bi-Taʿrīf Ḥuqūq al-Muṣṭafā of Qadi Iyad al-Yahsubi (d. 544/1149), the Andalusian-Maghribi Maliki judge — the classical work on the Prophet's qualities and the rights owed to him, and the natural reference for a Maliki scholar on this subject. The title is left transliterated and not translated, per the corpus convention for named works. The source writes القاضى with a dotless yāʾ.

options: read as البرية, 'creation', as the same phrase is spelled correctly earlier in the record
flags.note: Source typo: البربة for البرية. The phrase خير البرية, 'the best of creation', appears correctly two headings above. Preserved and flagged. The record also writes الإحتجاج with hamzat qaṭʿ for الاحتجاج.

translator_notes: A news-desk report consisting mostly of a list of the lecture's headings. Not one of the fourteen headings is developed, and the lecture itself exists only as the recording the record points to.
The CMS timestamp, 22 September 2012, is a bulk-upload date; the body dates the lecture to the evening of Friday 5 Dhu al-Qa'dah 1433 / 21 September 2012.

'نصرة' is rendered 'support' throughout; it covers giving aid, taking someone's part and coming to their defence, and in the phrase نصرة رسول الله it is the standing term for defending the Prophet's honour. 'Defence' was rejected as narrowing it.
'التابعين' is rendered 'the Successors', the generation after the Companions.
The record belongs with 805, the fatwa summary of four days earlier, and should not be displayed apart from it.
